Because the document says "most" and never identifies which analyses are the prespecified ones and which are the ad hoc ones, no individual outcome in this record can be marked prespecified=yes from this document. All nine prespecified conflicts therefore resolve to "unclear".

Tier conflicts are decided on the same weak footing but in the opposite direction: the document explicitly calls the whole report "secondary analyses of the trials", and the word "exploratory" does not appear anywhere in the text. Maintainers should note the residual ambiguity — the acknowledgement that "some ad hoc analyses" are included means an individual analysis (plausibly the proportional hazards risk-factor model, which is presented without any prespecification claim) could in fact be ad hoc. If the schema admits a distinct "ad hoc" or "unclear" tier value, that would be a more faithful encoding than either reading offered here.

Conflicts #0 and #1 are not close calls: both harms are reported with explicit numerators and percentages in Table 1 and in the Results narrative. For macrohemorrhage the document's own wording is "Hemorrhage >1 cm" / "Larger brain hemorrhages measuring more than 1 cm in diameter" rather than "macrohemorrhage"; the record should keep the document's phrasing if harm labels are meant to be verbatim.
